source.name: DAMA-DMBOK2 Revised Edition (2024)
source.status: Activity groupings summarise DMBOK2's context diagrams in the maintainers' own words. They are not quotations, and have not been checked line by line against the book.

areas.name: Data governance
areas.desc: Who decides about data, and how: ownership, stewardship, policy, ethics and maturity. DAMA puts it at the centre of the wheel because it steers every other area.

areas.name: Data architecture
areas.desc: The overall design of an organisation's data estate: platforms, lakes, meshes and the blueprints that connect them.

areas.name: Data modelling and design
areas.desc: Describing what data means and how it fits together: models, schemas and ontologies.

areas.name: Data storage and operations
areas.desc: Running the databases and stores that hold data: provisioning, migration, backup and performance.

areas.name: Data security and privacy
areas.desc: Keeping data safe and lawful: protecting personal data, pseudonymising, controlling access and creating safe synthetic data.

areas.name: Data integration and interoperability
areas.desc: Moving and combining data between systems: pipelines, orchestration, transformation, streaming and exchange.

areas.name: Document and content management
areas.desc: Looking after documents, records and web content, including archives and digital preservation.

areas.name: Reference and master data
areas.desc: Shared lists and records everyone should agree on: code lists, registers, addresses and organisations, and matching records about the same thing.

areas.name: Data warehousing and business intelligence
areas.desc: Bringing data together for analysis and decisions: warehouses, dashboards, reports and analytical publishing.

areas.name: Metadata management
areas.desc: Describing data so it can be found, understood and trusted: catalogues, dictionaries, lineage and metadata standards.

areas.name: Data quality
areas.desc: Whether data is fit for use: profiling it, testing it against rules, monitoring it over time, and fixing it.

areas.name: Data handling ethics
areas.desc: How data is used fairly and transparently, beyond what the law requires: DMBOK2 chapter 2.

areas.name: Big data and data science
areas.desc: Exploring large and varied data, building and running models, and putting their results to work: DMBOK2 chapter 14.

areas.name: Data management maturity assessment
areas.desc: Measuring how well data is managed, to plan and track improvement: DMBOK2 chapter 15.

areas.name: Data management organisation and roles
areas.desc: The structures, roles and skills that do data management: DMBOK2 chapter 16.

areas.name: Data management and organisational change
areas.desc: Helping people adopt new ways of managing data: DMBOK2 chapter 17.

activities.name: Define data governance for the organisation
activities.what: Agree what governance must achieve here, its scope and who sponsors it, after assessing readiness and current pain points.
activities.deliverables: Governance charter; readiness assessment; scope statement
activities.roles: Chief data officer; senior sponsor; data governance lead
activities.techniques: Readiness and culture assessment; stakeholder mapping
activities.metrics: Sponsor engagement; scope agreed and signed off

activities.name: Develop the data governance strategy
activities.what: Set the goals, principles, roadmap and benefits case for governance, aligned to the organisation's strategy.
activities.deliverables: Governance strategy and roadmap; benefits case

activities.name: Define the operating model
activities.what: Decide the bodies, decision rights, escalation paths and cadence: centralised, federated or hybrid.
activities.deliverables: Operating model; terms of reference; RACI
activities.roles: Data governance council; data owners; data stewards
activities.metrics: Decisions taken within agreed time; escalations resolved

activities.name: Write principles, policies and standards
activities.what: Turn the strategy into policies and standards people can follow, and the procedures that apply them.
activities.roles: Data governance lead; data owners; legal and information rights
activities.techniques: Policy drafting and consultation; standards adoption
activities.metrics: Policies published and current; exceptions recorded

activities.name: Appoint and support data owners and stewards
activities.what: Name accountable owners and working stewards for each data domain, and give them time, training and tools.
activities.deliverables: Ownership register; steward role profiles; training plan
activities.roles: Data owners; data stewards; HR and learning
activities.techniques: Domain mapping; role profiles; communities of practice
activities.metrics: Domains with a named owner and steward

activities.name: Manage data issues
activities.what: Log, triage and resolve data issues and disputes through the operating model, and learn from them.
activities.metrics: Issues open and their age; repeat issues

activities.name: Assess regulatory compliance
activities.what: Identify the laws and rules data must meet (UK GDPR, Data Protection Act 2018, FOI, records law, sector rules) and check compliance.
activities.roles: Data protection officer; information rights; audit
activities.metrics: Compliance findings closed; DPIAs completed before change

activities.name: Implement and embed governance
activities.what: Roll governance out in stages, fund data management work, and make it part of how projects and services run.
activities.roles: Programme and project boards; data governance lead
activities.metrics: Projects passing data checkpoints; adoption measures

activities.name: Value data as an asset
activities.what: Record what data the organisation holds, what it is worth and what it costs, and use that to set priorities.
activities.deliverables: Information asset register; valuation; critical data list
activities.roles: Information asset owners; finance; data owners
activities.techniques: Asset registers; critical data elements; valuation methods
activities.metrics: Assets registered with an owner; critical data identified

activities.name: Measure and report governance
activities.what: Track whether governance works, with metrics for adoption, compliance, value and quality, and report them.

activities.name: Establish the data architecture practice
activities.what: Set up the role, scope and methods of data architecture, and how it works with enterprise and solution architecture.

activities.name: Understand business strategy and requirements
activities.what: Translate strategy and business needs into the data the organisation needs, now and in future.

activities.name: Develop the enterprise data model
activities.what: Model the organisation's main data subjects and their relationships, from conceptual down to logical level.
activities.deliverables: Enterprise data model; subject area model

activities.name: Design data flows and integration architecture
activities.what: Map how data moves between systems and organisations, and choose patterns for integration and sharing.

activities.name: Design data platforms
activities.what: Choose and design the platforms that store and serve data: warehouses, lakes, lakehouses, and the cloud services under them.
activities.roles: Data and cloud architects; platform engineers

activities.name: Design data products and domain ownership
activities.what: Organise data as products owned by domains, with contracts for how others can use them (data mesh and similar).
activities.metrics: Data products with owners and contracts

activities.name: Govern architecture change
activities.what: Review designs against standards and the target architecture, and keep the roadmap current.

activities.name: Plan data modelling
activities.what: Decide which models are needed, their notation, naming standards and where they are kept.
activities.techniques: Modelling standards; notation choice (IE, UML, IDEF1X)

activities.name: Build conceptual models
activities.what: Describe the main things the business works with and how they relate, in business terms.

activities.name: Build logical models
activities.what: Add attributes, keys and rules, normalised and independent of any technology.

activities.name: Build physical models and schemas
activities.what: Turn logical models into database, file or message schemas for a chosen technology.
activities.deliverables: DDL; JSON Schema; XML Schema; Avro or Protobuf schemas

activities.name: Model dimensional and analytical structures
activities.what: Design star and snowflake schemas, facts and dimensions for analysis and reporting.

activities.name: Model semantics: ontologies and vocabularies
activities.what: Describe meaning formally, with ontologies, vocabularies and knowledge graphs, so data can be linked and reasoned over.
activities.techniques: RDF, OWL, SKOS, SHACL; linked data

activities.name: Review, version and manage models
activities.what: Review models for quality, keep versions, and keep them in step with the systems they describe.
activities.techniques: Model reviews; version control; reverse engineering

activities.name: Plan database technology
activities.what: Choose database and storage technologies for each need: relational, document, graph, search, time series or object storage.
activities.techniques: Technology appraisal; total cost of ownership

activities.name: Build and deploy databases
activities.what: Create databases and storage with infrastructure as code, sized and secured for their use.

activities.name: Manage schema change and migration
activities.what: Change schemas safely, migrate data between versions or platforms, and keep environments in step.

activities.name: Operate, monitor and tune databases
activities.what: Keep databases available and fast: monitoring, capacity, tuning and patching.

activities.name: Back up and recover data
activities.what: Back data up, test restores, and plan for continuity and disaster recovery.
activities.deliverables: Backup policy; recovery tests; continuity plans
activities.metrics: Recovery point and time objectives met

activities.name: Retain, archive and purge data
activities.what: Keep data as long as needed, move it to cheaper storage, and delete it when its retention period ends.

activities.name: Identify security and privacy requirements
activities.what: Work out what law, policy and risk require: classification, privacy, retention and who may see what.

activities.name: Define data security policy and standards
activities.what: Set policy for access, encryption, logging, retention and sharing, and the standards that apply it.

activities.name: Classify and discover sensitive data
activities.what: Find personal and sensitive data wherever it is, and label it.

activities.name: Control access
activities.what: Grant and review access by role and need to know, with strong authentication and least privilege.
activities.roles: Identity and access management team; data owners
activities.techniques: Role- and attribute-based access control; single sign-on
activities.metrics: Access reviews done; excess privileges removed

activities.name: Protect data: encryption, masking and de-identification
activities.what: Encrypt data, mask or tokenise it, and anonymise or pseudonymise it for wider use.
activities.metrics: Data protected at rest and in transit

activities.name: Create synthetic data
activities.what: Generate data that keeps useful patterns without revealing real people, for testing and research.
activities.deliverables: Synthetic datasets; utility and disclosure reports

activities.name: Provide secure data environments
activities.what: Give researchers and analysts governed access to sensitive data in trusted research environments.

activities.name: Monitor, audit and respond
activities.what: Log and audit data access, detect misuse, and respond to breaches.
activities.metrics: Incidents detected and reported within 72 hours

activities.name: Plan integration and interoperability
activities.what: Decide how systems and organisations will exchange data: patterns, standards and the integration architecture.

activities.name: Design and build pipelines (ETL and ELT)
activities.what: Extract, load and transform data between sources and targets.

activities.name: Orchestrate and schedule
activities.what: Run pipelines in the right order and at the right time, and recover from failure.
activities.metrics: Runs on time; mean time to recover

activities.name: Stream and process events
activities.what: Move and process data continuously as events happen, with messaging and stream processing.
activities.techniques: Publish–subscribe; change data capture; stream processing

activities.name: Publish and consume APIs
activities.what: Expose and use data through APIs, with documentation, versioning and security.
activities.deliverables: APIs; OpenAPI descriptions; API catalogue entries

activities.name: Share data between organisations
activities.what: Agree, set up and run data sharing with other bodies, lawfully and with clear terms.

activities.name: Replicate and virtualise
activities.what: Copy data between stores, or present data from many stores as one, without moving it.

activities.name: Monitor integration
activities.what: Watch pipelines, interfaces and exchanges for failure, delay and drift.

activities.name: Plan records and content management
activities.what: Decide what records and content must be kept, how they are organised and the rules that apply.
activities.deliverables: Records management policy; file plan; retention schedule

activities.name: Capture and manage documents
activities.what: Capture documents into a managed store, index them and control versions.

activities.name: Manage web and published content
activities.what: Create, approve and publish content for websites and intranets, and keep it current.
activities.deliverables: Content management system; content model; style guide

activities.name: Organise with taxonomies
activities.what: Organise documents and content with taxonomies, controlled vocabularies and metadata for findability.

activities.name: Retain, preserve and dispose of records
activities.what: Keep records for their retention period, preserve those of lasting value, and dispose of the rest.
activities.deliverables: Disposal records; transfers to archives; digital preservation
activities.metrics: Records disposed on schedule; transfers made

activities.name: Respond to information requests and legal holds
activities.what: Find and produce information for FOI, subject access, inquiries and legal discovery.

activities.name: Identify drivers and requirements
activities.what: Find which reference and master data the organisation depends on and what problems duplicates and inconsistency cause.
activities.deliverables: Requirements; scope of master data domains

activities.name: Manage reference data and code lists
activities.what: Keep code lists and classifications authoritative, versioned and available to everyone who needs them.

activities.name: Manage master data
activities.what: Keep one trusted version of core records (people, organisations, places, products) across systems.
activities.deliverables: Master data hub or register; golden records
activities.metrics: Duplicate rate; systems using the master

activities.name: Match, link and resolve entities
activities.what: Find records that are the same thing across sources, and link or merge them.

activities.name: Manage addresses and location identifiers
activities.what: Use authoritative identifiers for property, streets and places, such as UPRN and USRN.
activities.deliverables: Address and location data; identifier lookups

activities.name: Govern and publish master and reference data
activities.what: Operate change control for master and reference data, and publish it for reuse.

activities.name: Understand requirements for analysis
activities.what: Find out which decisions, questions and reports the warehouse and BI must support.

activities.name: Design and build the warehouse or lakehouse
activities.what: Design and build the analytical store: layers, models and loading.
activities.techniques: Kimball, Inmon, data vault; medallion layers

activities.name: Develop reports and dashboards
activities.what: Build the reports and dashboards people use to see what is happening.

activities.name: Produce statistics and reproducible analysis
activities.what: Produce official and analytical outputs with reproducible, quality-assured pipelines.

activities.name: Enable self-service analytics
activities.what: Let people answer their own questions with governed, documented data and tools.

activities.name: Operate and tune the warehouse and BI
activities.what: Keep loads, refreshes and reports running, fast and trusted.

activities.name: Define the metadata strategy
activities.what: Decide which metadata matters, who owns it, and how it is collected and used.

activities.name: Define the metadata architecture and standards
activities.what: Choose metadata standards and how metadata is stored, exchanged and linked.
activities.deliverables: Metadata model; exchange standards (DCAT, Dublin Core)

activities.name: Build data catalogues
activities.what: Describe data assets so people can find, understand and request them.
activities.metrics: Assets catalogued; searches that find something

activities.name: Maintain business glossaries and data dictionaries
activities.what: Define business terms and data elements consistently, and link them to the data.

activities.name: Capture lineage and impact
activities.what: Record where data comes from, how it changes and where it goes, to support trust and impact analysis.

activities.name: Integrate, distribute and use metadata
activities.what: Harvest metadata from systems automatically, keep it current and share it with other catalogues.

activities.name: Govern metadata quality
activities.what: Check metadata is complete, correct and current, and fix it when it is not.

activities.name: Define high-quality data and the DQ strategy
activities.what: Agree what good enough means for each use, and the strategy and roles for getting there.

activities.name: Identify critical data and business rules
activities.what: Find the data that matters most and the rules it must follow.
activities.techniques: Critical data element identification; rule capture

activities.name: Profile and assess quality
activities.what: Measure data against the rules and dimensions to find what is wrong and how much.
activities.techniques: Profiling; dimension scoring (completeness, accuracy, timeliness, validity, uniqueness, consistency)

activities.name: Validate and test data
activities.what: Check data automatically as it is created and moved, and stop or flag what fails.

activities.name: Cleanse and standardise
activities.what: Correct, standardise and enrich data, and remove duplicates.

activities.name: Monitor quality and observability
activities.what: Watch quality continuously and alert when it drifts or breaks.

activities.name: Manage quality issues and root causes
activities.what: Track quality issues to their root cause and fix the process, not just the data.

activities.name: Report quality and improve
activities.what: Report quality to owners and users, and plan improvements.

activities.name: Set ethical principles for data use
activities.what: Agree the values and principles that guide how data and algorithms are used.

activities.name: Assess ethical risk
activities.what: Assess projects for fairness, transparency, accountability and public benefit.

activities.name: Be transparent about algorithms
activities.what: Publish how algorithmic tools are used in decisions that affect people.

activities.name: Detect and mitigate bias
activities.what: Test data and models for bias, and reduce it.

activities.name: Define the data science strategy and use cases
activities.what: Decide where data science and AI can help, and how success is measured.

activities.name: Acquire and prepare big data
activities.what: Bring in large and varied data and prepare it for analysis.

activities.name: Explore and model
activities.what: Explore data and build statistical, machine learning or AI models.

activities.name: Deploy and monitor models (MLOps)
activities.what: Put models into service, monitor drift and performance, and retrain.

activities.name: Visualise and communicate results
activities.what: Show results clearly and accessibly, with their uncertainty.

activities.name: Choose a maturity model
activities.what: Pick a model and scale that fit the organisation, and agree the scope of the assessment.
activities.techniques: Maturity models (DAMA, CMMI DMM, government data maturity)

activities.name: Assess current maturity
activities.what: Gather evidence and score current practice in each area.

activities.name: Plan improvement
activities.what: Set target maturity and the roadmap to reach it.

activities.name: Reassess and track
activities.what: Repeat the assessment to measure progress.

activities.name: Design the data organisation
activities.what: Choose how data management is organised: centralised, decentralised, federated or networked.

activities.name: Define roles and skills
activities.what: Describe data roles and the skills they need, and build a skills plan.

activities.name: Build data literacy
activities.what: Help everyone understand and use data well.

activities.name: Plan change for data management
activities.what: Plan how people will be brought into new data practices and tools.

activities.name: Communicate and support adoption
activities.what: Communicate the why, train people and support them while habits change.
